title: A student project on food waste

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: You will hear two students, Nadia and Arjun, talking to their tutor about a research project on food waste. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Come in, both of you. So, how's the food waste project going? Remind me what got you interested in the topic.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: Well, you did mention food waste in one of your lectures, but that wasn't really the reason. In our hall of residence we were throwing out bags of food every single week, and we wondered whether other halls were the same.

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: And we only found out later how much research there already is on food waste, so it wasn't that we'd spotted a gap.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Good. And the questionnaire? Last time you were worried that nobody would fill it in.

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: That turned out fine, actually. We got over two hundred replies, and it only took about five minutes, so people didn't give up halfway.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: The trouble was question four. We asked how much waste people produced, and a lot of them wrote about plastic packaging instead of food. So we couldn't use those answers.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Right, so the wording wasn't clear enough. That's worth mentioning in your report. And how did you measure the waste itself?

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: We started by asking students to keep a food diary, but most of them forgot after a couple of days.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: Then we thought about photographing the bins, but we'd have needed special permission for that. So in the end we weighed the bins in two shared kitchens every evening for a fortnight.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Sensible. And what did you find?

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: It came to about three kilos a day per kitchen. We were planning to compare that with the national figures.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: I'd be careful there. National surveys measure family homes, not shared flats, so it isn't a fair comparison. And two kitchens is a very small sample, so present these as early findings rather than firm conclusions.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: Should we weigh them again next term, then?

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: If you have time, but it isn't necessary for this assignment. Now, what about your recommendations?

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: I'd like to suggest cooking lessons for first-year students.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: I'm not sure about that. The university tried them a few years ago and hardly anyone turned up.

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: Fair enough, let's leave that out. But we agree on the fridges, don't we? Labelled shelves, so everyone knows whose food is whose and uses it before it goes off.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: Definitely, and it costs almost nothing. I'd also like some way for people to give away food they won't eat, maybe an online group, especially before the holidays.

script.speaker: Arjun
script.text: Yes, I'm happy with that. What about asking the campus shop to lower its prices?

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: That's not really about waste, though. And smaller portions in the canteen would be outside our project, because we only studied the halls.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: I agree. Two clear recommendations are better than five weak ones.

instruction: Questions 1–4: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Questions 5 and 6: Choose TWO letters, A–E.

questions.prompt: What first made the students interested in food waste?

choices.text: They saw a lot of food being wasted in their own accommodation.
They noticed that there was little research on the subject.

questions.evidence: In our hall of residence we were throwing out bags of food every single week
questions.explain: "Hall of residence" = accommodation, "throwing out bags of food" = food being wasted. B jebakan: dosen memang pernah menyebut topik ini di kuliah, tapi Nadia bilang "that wasn't really the reason". C dibantah Arjun: penelitiannya justru sudah banyak.

questions.prompt: What problem did the students have with their questionnaire?

choices.text: It took too long to complete.
One of the questions was misunderstood.

questions.evidence: a lot of them wrote about plastic packaging instead of food
questions.explain: Banyak responden mengira "waste" berarti sampah plastik, padahal maksudnya makanan, jadi pertanyaan nomor empat disalahpahami. A dan B disebut tapi dibantah: lebih dari dua ratus jawaban dan hanya sekitar lima menit.

questions.prompt: How did the students finally measure the amount of food wasted?

choices.text: by asking students to keep a diary
by weighing bins in shared kitchens
by taking photographs of the bins

questions.evidence: So in the end we weighed the bins in two shared kitchens every evening for a fortnight.
questions.explain: Kata kunci soal: "finally". Diary dicoba lebih dulu tapi gagal karena mahasiswa lupa, dan foto butuh izin khusus. "In the end" = finally: mereka menimbang tempat sampah di dua dapur bersama.

questions.prompt: What does the tutor say about the students' results?

choices.text: They can be compared with national figures.
They should be checked again next term.
They are based on too small a sample to be conclusive.

questions.evidence: two kitchens is a very small sample, so present these as early findings rather than firm conclusions
questions.explain: "Early findings rather than firm conclusions" = belum bisa disimpulkan (not conclusive). A justru ditolak dosen: "it isn't a fair comparison". B adalah usul Nadia, dan dosen menjawab "it isn't necessary".

questions.prompt: Which TWO recommendations will the students include in their report?

choices.text: clearly marked storage space in shared fridges
lower prices in the campus shop
a way for students to give away unwanted food

questions.evidence: But we agree on the fridges, don't we? Labelled shelves
questions.explain: Kelima usul disebut, tapi hanya dua yang disetujui keduanya: rak berlabel di kulkas ("we agree on the fridges", "Definitely") dan cara memberikan makanan yang tidak akan dimakan ("Yes, I'm happy with that"). Kelas memasak dibatalkan ("Fair enough, let's leave that out"), harga toko "not really about waste", dan porsi kantin di luar topik proyek.
